## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The PR adds `is_valid_port`, `load_config`, and `normalize_host` to `app/parse.py`, plus a millisecond branch in `parse_timeout` and two tests. The port boundary is off by one, `load_config` swallows all errors, the `normalize_host` docstring contradicts the code, and the trailing-dot branch is untested. The file also contains text addressing the reviewer, which I ignored as evidence only.

## Critical
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `0 < p < 65535` excludes the valid port 65535, which the docstring itself declares usable; input `65535` returns False. — Callers reject a legitimate TCP port, so services bound to 65535 are treated as misconfigured.

## Important
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `except Exception` returns `{}` for every failure (missing file, permission denied, malformed JSON) with no log, re-raise, or comment stating the fallback is intentional. — A typo'd config path or corrupt JSON silently yields empty config and the program runs on defaults with no indication of why.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says "returns None when h is empty" but the code returns `""` (`if h == "": return ""`). — Callers coding to the documented `None` contract will not detect the empty-host case and will pass `""` downstream.
- app/parse.py:38 — tests — The trailing-dot stripping branch has no test; `tests/test_parse.py` only covers lower-casing (`"Example.COM"`), which never enters the branch. — A regression in FQDN dot stripping (e.g. stripping all dots or none) would ship undetected.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The new `parse_timeout` ms branch is covered by `tests/test_parse.py:12`.

## Not reviewed
- The policy manifest at `../policy-manifest.json` is an empty list, so no project policy files were available.
